workstream: B03 probe: can the ResourcefulLib registration path carry a registry key?

checks.why: the wrapper's register() only collects entries; the key cannot be injected there
init() is empty, so registration is not deferred to init
FabricRegistryEntry.of is the only place that both calls the supplier and registers
the id must be readable (local 1) before Supplier.get(), or no context can be set

injectionPoint.whatToInsert: aload_1 (the Identifier local) + a bridge call that stores it as the pending registry id in a ThreadLocal
injectionPoint.whyItWorks: the supplier is evaluated inside this method, so a lambda that builds Item.Settings runs with the pending id set

whatIsStillMissing: a rule type that inserts a call before a matched call (the existing registrationKeys rule only fires when a register call is in the SAME method as the settings ctor)
a bridge that exposes the pending id and a settings factory
a second rule to redirect the mod's `new Item.Settings()` inside the lambda
ThreadLocal lifetime handling: nested registrations or an exception would leak the id
scope: probe only: nothing was patched. This answers 'is there an injection point', not 'does the conversion work'.
